about: Every change to this repo, newest last. Fields: id, date, commit_message, summary, files, changes (what and how), bugs_fixed (symptom, cause, fix), notes.

entries.commit_message: feat: stage 1 course database (parser, SQLite, throttled cached fetcher, manual-login session, importers, quality report)
entries.summary: Stage 1: parse the Spring 2027 registrar schedule into a local SQLite database, with Core curriculum tags.

changes.how: selectolax (lexbor) reads table.results; rows are matched by their data-th header text, course headers (td.course_header h2) are split into dept, number and title with a regex, and each section is validated by a strict Pydantic Section model. Per-row failures are recorded, not fatal.
timeutil.parse_days uses a TH|M|T|W|F|S|U regex and rejects leftovers; parse_time_range converts 'a.m./p.m.' ranges to minutes from midnight and rejects end <= start.

db.py creates course, section, meeting, instructor, section_instructor, section_tag, core_area, crawl_log, parse_failure and requirement_group tables. Upsert replaces scalar fields and meetings but unions tags and instructors, and keeps an existing level when a new source lacks one.

fetch.Fetcher caches by sha256 of the URL under data/cache, waits at least 3 seconds between live requests, backs off exponentially on network errors and 5xx, and raises BlockedError on 403, 429 or CAPTCHA text and SessionExpired on a redirect to the UT login.

session.login opens a headed Playwright Chromium, waits for the schedule search page, then saves cookies only (storage_state, mode 600) to data/session/. clear-session deletes that folder. The code never reads credentials.
crawl.plan builds 10 Core-area searches plus every field of study x L/U/G from the home-page select (229 fields), following next_unique pagination links.
import-html parses pages saved from the browser; import-json validates a list of Sections; quality.report prints counts, parse failures, missing times and tag coverage.

23 pytest tests covering time parsing (plus a Hypothesis round trip), parsing, DB upserts, the JSON importer rejecting malformed input, crawl planning and the fetcher's cache, throttle, block and session-expiry behavior.

bugs_fixed.fix: format times with printf('%d:%02d-%d:%02d', ...)

bugs_fixed.fix: assert exactly 229

bugs_fixed.fix: removed the re-raise, caught ValueError/KeyError in the parser and PlaywrightError in login, used pydantic ValidationError in tests

bugs_fixed.fix: git rm --cached and added __pycache__ to .gitignore

notes: The registrar schedule requires UT login; UT's acceptable-use policy (sections 5.7, 5.10) does not clearly permit scripted access. The user chose the automated crawl and accepts the account risk.
Verified against one real saved page only (Core area 090, 40 sections, 0 parse failures). Department result pages and non-core flags are unverified until the first real crawl.

entries.commit_message: fix: login command hung after manual login
entries.summary: The login command never saved the session after the user logged in, so the terminal stayed blocked.

changes.what: Login detection based on URL and page title
changes.how: is_schedule_page() returns true when the host is utdirect.utexas.edu, the path contains /course_schedule/, and the title contains 'Course Search', 'Search Results' or 'Course Schedule'. It is unit tested against schedule, login and unrelated URLs.
The poll loop checks stdin with select(); pressing Enter saves the session if the browser is on the utdirect host, and prints a message if it is still on the login host.

bugs_fixed.symptom: After logging in, 'uv run utcoursesplus login' kept waiting and the terminal could not be used for the next command
bugs_fixed.cause: The old check required the text 'Search for' within the first 400 characters of the page body, and the page title does not contain it, so the check never became true
bugs_fixed.fix: Replaced it with the URL and title check above, plus the Enter fallback. Ctrl+C on the old version discards the login, so re-run login with the new code.

notes: Playwright cannot be run in this cloud container, so the new loop is covered by unit tests of the detection function only, not an end-to-end browser run.

entries.commit_message: fix: keep unrecognized Core tags visible; add reparse and diagnose commands
entries.summary: The first real crawl (C S + Mathematics core) showed 237 sections with a Core tag but only 102 mapped to a named Core area, no flags at all, 37 sections without times and 68 without instructors. Added tools to rebuild from cached pages and to dump the raw rows behind the anomalies.

changes.how: Labels are matched to the 10 Core areas after normalizing case, punctuation and '&' vs 'and'. A tag whose tooltip says 'core curriculum requirement' but is not one of the 10 is stored as kind=core, code='unmapped'. Everything else is a flag. The tooltip text is now stored in section_tag.title.

A table row with no unique number but with days, hours or instructors is attached to the section above it as an extra meeting or instructor. This guards against multi-meeting sections being truncated; it is based on an assumption and will be confirmed or removed from the diagnose output.
rebuild.reparse_cache deletes sections that came from the authenticated crawl and re-parses every page in data/cache, using the URL's level and core_code. It makes no network requests.
rebuild.diagnose writes up to 3 raw HTML rows each for sections with no times, no instructors, rows with no unique number, and each unusual tag label to data/diagnose.txt.
Added missing_times_by_mode, no_instructor_by_status, unmapped_core_labels and flag_titles; removed the old flags counter.
connect() drops and recreates section_tag when it lacks the title column; the table is derived data and reparse restores it.

bugs_fixed.symptom: sections_with_core_tag was 237 but the named Core areas totalled 102, and flags was empty
bugs_fixed.cause: Any tag with 'core curriculum requirement' in its tooltip and a label that did not exactly match my area names was stored as a core tag under its CSS class, so it was counted nowhere and hidden
bugs_fixed.fix: Unrecognized core-titled tags are stored as code 'unmapped' and listed by label in the quality report; label matching is now normalized

notes: Cause of the 37 sections without times and 68 without instructors is not yet known. They may be asynchronous online sections, staff-taught sections, or multi-row sections. Run diagnose and send data/diagnose.txt to confirm.
28 tests pass. Not run against the user's cached pages, which live only on their machine.

entries.commit_message: refactor: drop unneeded continuation-row parsing; report empty pages
entries.summary: Real crawl output showed no multi-row sections, so the speculative continuation-row code is removed. Anomalies from the first crawl were explained by the data, not the parser.

changes.how: diagnose found 0 rows without a unique number in 292 sections, so the assumption was unsupported; the test for it was replaced with one built from the real markup.
Added empty_page_urls and by_mode.

bugs_fixed.symptom: Earlier report showed 237 sections with Core tags vs 102 in named areas
bugs_fixed.cause:
The registrar emits empty placeholder
  • on sections with no Core area; the first parser counted them as core tags
bugs_fixed.fix: Entries with an empty label are skipped (done in 6b6bb14); verified: sections_with_core_tag is now 102 and unmapped_core_labels is empty. A test using the real markup now covers it.

notes: 37 sections without times are real: 24 Internet sections and 13 face-to-face research/reading courses with no meeting time. 68 sections have an empty instructor cell (staff/TBA). The schedule generator in Stage 5 must handle sections with no meeting time and no instructor.
No non-Core flags (writing, ethics, global cultures, etc.) appear in the C S results, so they may only exist on each section's detail page. A saved detail page is needed to confirm.

entries.commit_message: feat: preferences, language-model tuning, ratings and grades import, shrinkage estimates
entries.summary: Stages 3 and 5 foundations: PreferenceConfig with validation and undo history, natural-language tuning that only edits the config, optional signal imports, and empirical-Bayes difficulty estimates with intervals.

changes.how: Pydantic models with extra='forbid'. Hard constraints (times, days off, gaps, walking, credit range, exclusions, required courses) and eight soft weights that are renormalized to sum to 1 by a model validator; all-zero weights fall back to defaults. History is a table whose newest row is current; undo deletes it.

nlpref.propose sends the request plus the current config to the model through client.messages.parse with a Pydantic output schema. required_courses is removed from what the model sees and cannot be returned (HardCore vs HardConstraints). Python then validates, computes the real diff and attaches the user's phrase and the model's rationale per changed path. A clarifying question or tradeoff note is passed through instead of silently picking. Nothing is applied until the API's apply call.

CSV importers validate every row and report rejected lines. Ratings are never scraped: RateMyProfessors' terms (section 6) prohibit automated access, so only CSV import and a link-out are supported. Grade imports store a source name and licence note per file.

signals.py works on a z scale: each source adds precision n*tau^2/sigma^2, posterior mean is the precision-weighted z shrunk toward the department prior, and the interval is +/-1.96 sd mapped through the normal CDF to a 0-1 ease. Missing sources are dropped and the blend weights renormalized; rank values subtract half the interval width so low-confidence courses rank lower while staying visible.
pyproject sets line length 110 and ignores RUF012/UP046/UP047, which flag Pydantic's literal defaults and generic helper signatures.

bugs_fixed.symptom: A test expected 3 ratings of difficulty 4.5 to stay above 0.2 ease
bugs_fixed.cause: The test assumed far-from-prior ratings are discounted more than they are; with a department prior near 2.0 the evidence really is strong
bugs_fixed.fix: Rewrote the test to compare the same rating at n=3 and n=300: the small sample must be pulled toward the prior and have a much wider interval

bugs_fixed.symptom: Rank values could go negative
bugs_fixed.cause: mean minus half-width is unbounded below
bugs_fixed.fix: Clip rank values to [0, 1]

bugs_fixed.symptom: Ambiguity guard in professor matching was always true
bugs_fixed.cause: Compared the set of distinct instructors with a list built from the same distinct keys
bugs_fixed.fix: Match only keys that map to exactly one imported person; two people sharing last name and first initial are skipped

notes: The model identifier defaults to claude-opus-5-5 and can be changed with the UTCP_MODEL environment variable. Refusals are reported as an error; server-side fallbacks are not enabled.
The spread constants (GPA_TAU, RMP_*_TAU and so on) are judgment values documented in signals.py, not fitted to UT data.

UT's official grade dashboard is at reports.utexas.edu/spotlight-data/ut-course-grade-distributions; licensing for reuse of exported data is not stated there, so the importer records a licence note per file.

entries.commit_message: feat: syllabus extraction, schedule generator, API and CLI commands
entries.summary: Stage 4 and the engine of Stage 5: quote-verified syllabus extraction with a documented lightness score and gold-set tools; requirements and Core tree; conflict-free schedule search with explanations, backups and a registration checklist; FastAPI service and CLI commands.

changes.how: The model fills a strict Pydantic schema (client.messages.parse). verify_quotes then nulls every value whose quote is not found, case and whitespace insensitive, in the syllabus text, so unsupported guesses never reach the score. Only public URLs are fetched: robots.txt is checked, login-gated hosts are refused, PDFs are read locally with pypdf.

Nine components with fixed weights (exam count 0.20, exam weight 0.20, weekly hours 0.15, final 0.10, attendance 0.10, projects 0.10, participation 0.05, late policy 0.05, group work 0.05). Missing components are dropped and the rest renormalized; coverage is stored and shown. Every component's rule is a string returned to the UI.
gold-sheet writes a CSV of stored syllabi to fill by hand; gold-eval reports per-field labeled count, accuracy, false values and misses (numeric tolerance 5 points for weights, 1 hour for hours).

Backtracking over slots (required courses, choose-from groups, Core areas, then electives to reach the credit minimum), most constrained slot first, pairwise overlap checks, credit ceiling, and branch-and-bound on an optimistic utility. A node budget returns best-found results and flags truncation. Candidate sections per slot are capped at the best 14 by section-level utility.

Weighted mean of eight features in [0,1]; walking is dropped when data/buildings.csv is absent and the rest renormalized. Rank values for ease, lightness and quality subtract half the interval width, so low-confidence courses rank lower while remaining visible.

explain_vs lists the features with the largest weighted difference plus the sections that differ. backups picks alternates minimizing overlap with the top pick and each other. registration_plan scores scarcity from status, reserved seats, open alternatives and required status and attaches a fallback section; it is labeled a heuristic, and the registration time is typed in by the user.

FastAPI app with endpoints for status, sources, requirements, audit parsing (shown for correction, never stored), Core tree, courses, preferences with propose/apply/undo, schedule generation, suggestions and imports. New CLI commands: serve, import-ratings, import-grades, add-syllabus, gold-sheet, gold-eval.
Split into _request (throttle, backoff, block detection), get (text) and get_bytes (PDF) sharing the same safeguards.

bugs_fixed.symptom: NameError: timezone not defined in fetch.py after refactor
bugs_fixed.cause: ruff had rewritten timezone.utc to datetime.UTC and the new code still used timezone
bugs_fixed.fix: use UTC

bugs_fixed.symptom: Test for excluded section failed validation
bugs_fixed.cause: The config validator correctly requires 5-digit unique numbers; the test used '9'

bugs_fixed.symptom: A ratings CSV row 'Smith John' did not match 'SMITH, JOHN'
bugs_fixed.cause: Without a comma the name is read as 'First Last'; 'Smith John' is ambiguous by construction
bugs_fixed.fix: documented the accepted formats ('Last, First' or 'First Last') and fixed the test data

notes: Courses with a linked lab or discussion appear in the registrar schedule as separate rows; the generator does not know co-requisites and treats each as an independent course.
One course satisfies at most one Core slot in a schedule, even if it carries several Core tags.
The model call for syllabus, audit and preference parsing uses client.messages.parse; refusals and SDK errors are returned as plain-language API errors.

entries.commit_message: feat: web interface, schedule list de-duplication, clearer credit-limit message
entries.summary: Stage 6: Vite + React + TypeScript interface with six screens, a hand-built weekly calendar, virtualized course table and a restrained design system; fixes found while running it against a synthetic database.

changes.how: Requirements (Core area checkboxes, required courses, per-area course options sorted easiest first, audit paste with review table), Courses and sections (virtualized with @tanstack/react-virtual, arrow-key navigation, detail panel with RMP link-out and source), Preferences (sliders, hard constraints, plain-English box with diff, phrases, reasons, apply and undo), Ranked schedules (calendar, why-this-ranks, score components, backups), Registration plan (hand-run checklist), Data sources (origins, missing signals, importers, syllabus form).

CSS variable tokens: one primary (deep blue), one accent (burnt orange), warm neutrals, light theme only, 2px radius, no gradients or shadows, IBM Plex Sans and Mono, a 12-24px type scale. scripts/contrast.mjs checks 16 token pairs against WCAG AA and the ratios are documented in styles.css. One icon library (lucide-react). Status is plain text with colour as reinforcement; uncertainty is shown as ranges and confidence words.

Skip link, visible focus ring, semantic table roles on the virtualized grid with aria-activedescendant, labels on every control, aria-live on result counts, responsive layout verified at 390px and 1440px.
generate now returns one schedule per distinct set of courses (best section choice); section-level alternatives stay in the pool and feed the backup schedules.

bugs_fixed.symptom: With requirements totalling 19 credit hours and a 18-hour maximum, the app said only that no combination fits
bugs_fixed.cause: The search pruned at the root and the generic message did not name the credit limit
bugs_fixed.fix: generate computes the minimum possible credit total first and reports 'Your requirements need at least N credit hours ... but your maximum is M'

bugs_fixed.symptom: The top eight schedules differed by a single section of the same courses
bugs_fixed.cause: The ranked list was the raw top of the pool
bugs_fixed.fix: De-duplicate by course set for the ranked list; keep the pool for backups

bugs_fixed.symptom: Phone layout scrolled sideways on every screen (about 500 px overflow)
bugs_fixed.cause: The one-column grid used 1fr, which lets wide tables stretch it
bugs_fixed.fix: minmax(0, 1fr) and min-width: 0 on main

bugs_fixed.symptom: Calendar hour labels wrapped in the compact view and the first label touched the header
bugs_fixed.cause: Labels were absolutely positioned at the edge and included a.m./p.m.
bugs_fixed.fix: Compact labels drop the suffix; the first label is nudged down

bugs_fixed.symptom: '1 courses offered'
bugs_fixed.cause: No plural handling
bugs_fixed.fix: Singular and plural text

bugs_fixed.symptom: Courses table needed sideways scrolling to see ease and difficulty at 1440 px
bugs_fixed.cause: Eleven columns summed past the content width
bugs_fixed.fix: Removed the room column (room is in the detail panel and calendar) and narrowed the rest

notes: The interface was exercised only against a synthetic database (backend/tests/demo_db.py) with headless Chromium: all six screens loaded at 1440 and 390 px with no console errors, failed requests or horizontal overflow. It has not been run against your crawled data.
Not exercised live: the language-model features (no API key in the build environment) and the Playwright login window (needs a display). The model calls are covered by tests with a stand-in client.
Keyboard navigation inside the courses grid and the Enter-to-save login fallback were written but not checked by hand.
